headline: BCB announces 15-member ODI squad for Zimbabwe tour
summary: Mehedi Hasan Miraz will lead the side as the Tigers prepare for a three-match series starting July 6.
details: The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has announced a 15-member squad for the upcoming three-match ODI series in Zimbabwe.
Mehedi Hasan Miraz has been named captain, with Nazmul Hossain Shanto as vice-captain.
The squad largely retains the team that won the recent series against Australia at home, with the exception of Sheikh Mahedi Hasan, who has been dropped.
Litton Das, who is sidelined from the only Test match of the tour due to injury, has been included in the ODI squad.
Bangladesh and Zimbabwe last faced each other in an ODI series in 2022, where the Tigers lost 2-1 as visitors in Zimbabwe.
The tour begins with a single Test match on June 28, followed by the ODI series from July 6, 9, and 11.

The full ODI squad includes: Mehedi Hasan Miraz (C), Nazmul Hossain Shanto (VC), Soumya Sarkar, Saif Hassan, Tanzid Hasan Tamim, Towhid Hridoy, Litton Das, Mosaddek Hossain Shaikat, Nurul Hasan Sohan, Rishad Hossain, Tanvir Islam, Mustafizur Rahman, Taskin Ahmed, Shoriful Islam, and Nahid Rana.
caption:
The Tigers are heading back to Zimbabwe! 🇧🇩🏏

The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has announced a 15-member squad for the upcoming three-match ODI series in Zimbabwe.

Mehedi Hasan Miraz has been named captain, with Nazmul Hossain Shanto as vice-captain.

The squad largely retains the team that won the recent series against Australia at home, with the exception of Sheikh Mahedi Hasan, who has been dropped.

Litton Das, who is sidelined from the only Test match of the tour due to injury, has been included in the ODI squad.

Bangladesh and Zimbabwe last faced each other in an ODI series in 2022, where the Tigers lost 2-1 as visitors in Zimbabwe.

The tour begins with a single Test match on June 28, followed by the ODI series from July 6, 9, and 11.

The full ODI squad includes: Mehedi Hasan Miraz (C), Nazmul Hossain Shanto (VC), Soumya Sarkar, Saif Hassan, Tanzid Hasan Tamim, Towhid Hridoy, Litton Das, Mosaddek Hossain Shaikat, Nurul Hasan Sohan, Rishad Hossain, Tanvir Islam, Mustafizur Rahman, Taskin Ahmed, Shoriful Islam, and Nahid Rana.

Source: Jamuna TV

headline_marked: AB Party calls for [[July organizers to play strong role]] in reforms
headline: AB Party calls for July organizers to play strong role in reforms
summary: Chairman Mojibur Rahman Manju urges unity among the forces of the July uprising to consolidate gains and build a future Bangladesh.
details: AB Party Chairman Mojibur Rahman Manju stated that the organizers of the July mass uprising must play a strong role in implementing state reforms to ensure the movement's goals are met.
During a meeting with various organizers at the party's central office in Bijoynagar, Dhaka, Manju noted that divisions have emerged over who gets credit for the movement.
He emphasized that instead of competing for credit, there should be a focus on self-reflection and regular communication among the forces of July to consolidate their achievements.
Manju further warned that the spirit of July should not be limited to mere formalities or be subjected to negative tagging, comparing its importance to the spirit of the Liberation War.
AB Party General Secretary Asaduzzaman Fuad added that the July uprising is not just a memory but the foundation for building a future Bangladesh, driven by the most conscious and educated youth.
Fuad stressed that the message of the July movement must reach the remotest areas of the country and that the new generation of warriors created by the 2024 movement must not fail.

Representatives from Inkilab Mancha also highlighted the need to better communicate the spirit of July to the general public through cultural and social activities to counter misinformation and trolling on social media.
caption:
Can the spirit of the July uprising be preserved? AB Party urges organizers to move past credit wars and lead state reforms.

AB Party Chairman Mojibur Rahman Manju stated that the organizers of the July mass uprising must play a strong role in implementing state reforms to ensure the movement's goals are met.

During a meeting with various organizers at the party's central office in Bijoynagar, Dhaka, Manju noted that divisions have emerged over who gets credit for the movement.

He emphasized that instead of competing for credit, there should be a focus on self-reflection and regular communication among the forces of July to consolidate their achievements.

Manju further warned that the spirit of July should not be limited to mere formalities or be subjected to negative tagging, comparing its importance to the spirit of the Liberation War.

AB Party General Secretary Asaduzzaman Fuad added that the July uprising is not just a memory but the foundation for building a future Bangladesh, driven by the most conscious and educated youth.

Fuad stressed that the message of the July movement must reach the remotest areas of the country and that the new generation of warriors created by the 2024 movement must not fail.

Representatives from Inkilab Mancha also highlighted the need to better communicate the spirit of July to the general public through cultural and social activities to counter misinformation and trolling on social media.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo
